description: Find the maximum value of f(x) and the real numbers x that achieve it.
guidelines: Zero credit for conjecturing the maximum value or optimal intervals without proof.
Zero credit for computing f(x) for small specific values of n without generalizing the algebraic step.
Zero credit for restating the problem in an equivalent form without making tangible progress toward bounding the sum.

The 1 point for evaluating the maximum value requires a fully correct evaluation. Minor cosmetic or arithmetic slips in this evaluation result in 0 points for that specific item (effectively a 1-point deduction).
If a student assumes without proof that the multiset of fractional parts for \gcd(\ell, n) > 1 is majorized by the coprime case, they earn at most 1 out of 2 points for the upper bound item.

children.description: Proves that f(x) is periodic with period 1 (i.e., f(x+1) = f(x)).
Shows that within any interval of the form [\ell/n, (\ell+1)/n) for integer \ell, f(x) is non-increasing.
Evaluates f(x) for the optimal range (e.g., testing x \in [1-1/n, 1) or x = (n-1)/n).
Explicitly calculates the candidate maximum value -1 + \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{k}.
Expresses the function algebraically in terms of fractional parts (e.g., deriving f(x) = \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\{kx\}}{k} - \{nx\}).

children.selection_signal: Proves the general upper bound for all integers \ell.

children.description: Proves the general upper bound \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\{k\ell/n\}}{k} \le \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{n-k}{nk} for all integers \ell.
Proves the general upper bound for all integers \ell.
